body.commentary:
The gender pay gap isn't closing. It's widening.

Despite the optimism many HR conversations carry — that pay equity is improving — the data tells a different story. As one expert put it plainly on a recent panel: «unfortunately, the gap is growing.» That's not a policy failure so much as a sign we're intervening in the wrong place.

Here's the trap: when we treat pay inequity as a solved problem and apply surface-level fixes, the underlying issue hardens and resurfaces as something bigger. In the US, for example, once pay equity becomes politicized, it stops being a workplace policy question and turns into a full-blown culture war.

For payroll and compensation decisions, the starting point can't be good intentions — it has to be measurable data. Otherwise every step we take to 'fix' the gap ends up entrenching it further.

What data is driving your organization's pay equity decisions?
